title: The Effect of the Short-Chain Fatty Acid Propionate in the Context of Arthritic Diseases
summary: The results of this study are expected to yield important conclusions and new insights into the functional role of gut bacteria and their metabolic products (including propionate) in the progression of autoimmune diseases.  Methodologically, the collected blood and stool samples are purified in scientific laboratories at Medical Clinic 3 in Erlangen and prepared for the corresponding analyses at Medical Clinic 3 using flow cytometry (to determine the proportions of specific immune cells) or next-generation sequencing (to unambiguously determine the composition of the gut microbiota) at Medical Clinic 3, and at the Institute of Biochemistry in Erlangen using gas chromatography coupled with mass spectrometry (to determine the metabolites of the gut microbiota).  At the start of the study, the diagnosis will be verified. On the day of the screening, a blood sample will be drawn, and you will provide a stool sample. You will then receive 56 high-fiber bars, which you will take twice daily. It is recommended that you take the bars in the afternoon. At the end of the study, another blood sample will be drawn, and you will provide another stool sample.

interventions.name: Patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) receive 2 propionate bars per day for 4 weeks. On Day 0 and Day 28, a blood sample is drawn as part of routine care, and a stool sample is submitted.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Rheumatoid Arthritis
Classification according to the 2010 ACR/EULAR classification criteria
Disease duration: no restriction
Treatment: no restriction on immunosuppressive therapy
Disease activity: no restriction
Adult, competent male or female individuals
Signed informed consent provided following prior instruction
Exclusion criteria:
Individuals who are unable to give informed consent and/or minors
Use of propionate as a dietary supplement 4 weeks prior to enrollment in
the study
